purpose: Assesses whether the organization can prevent or detect an adversary's attempts to gain an initial foothold into a system that uses AI, whether local, edge, or cloud-enabled.
summary: Initial Access consists of techniques that use various entry vectors to gain an initial foothold within a system that hosts or interacts with AI capabilities. Common vectors include AI supply chain compromise, exploiting public-facing applications, phishing, and abuse of valid accounts.
expectedStatementElements: How the organization vets the AI software/hardware/data supply chain before deployment
How public-facing applications that expose or interact with AI models are hardened and monitored
What controls prevent phishing-based initial access to systems with AI privileges
How valid account abuse is prevented, including protections against credential reuse and default credentials
evidenceExamples: AI supply chain vetting records (software, model, dataset, and hardware provenance checks)
Vulnerability scanning and patch management records for public-facing AI-enabled applications
Phishing simulation results and security awareness training records
MFA enforcement and conditional access policy configuration for accounts with AI system access
commonGaps: AI supply chain components (models, datasets, packages) are integrated without provenance verification
Public-facing applications exposing AI functionality aren't regularly scanned or patched
MFA isn't enforced consistently across accounts with access to AI systems, especially service accounts
interviewQuestions: How do we verify a third-party model or dataset isn't compromised before we use it?
How current is patching on public-facing applications that expose our AI functionality?
Is MFA enforced on every account type with access to our AI systems, including service accounts?
What happens when an employee clicks a phishing link targeting AI system credentials?
